review: Fresh independent literal-stem, answer-key and source-coverage challenge 05
scope: 1996 classic English base game, publisher PDF pp.1–12, every base Action Card; expansions pp.13–20, later editions and optional short game excluded
inputs_read: source_pdfs/el-grande-publisher-rules.pdf (pp.1–12 only; direct pypdf text extraction)
independence: No summaries, reader outputs, grades, other review reports or parent history were read. Names of earlier artifacts appearing inside the allowed ledger were not followed.

verdict.supported_source_target_saturation: NOT YET SATURATED: one proposed distinct starting-resource question remains outside the literal 53 stems and keys.
verdict.complete_core_gameplay: INCOMPLETE / NO PASS: essential legal-play branches lack a definitive resolution in the permitted source, independently of whether supported targets are saturated.

findings.finding: Each player receives the complete color-matched set of 13 power cards, numbered 1–13. None of Q01–Q53 literally asks for or requires the initial power-card hand. Q03 addresses what a played card determines, Q19 recovery, Q21 action stacks/round marker, and Q22 used-card handling; those do not establish which decision resources are initially available. The ledger maps the preparation passage to Q17/Q19/Q21/Q45 without this starting-state fact being tested.
findings.novelty: Initial supply of usable power cards is a distinct setup rule. It is not an alternate numeric recruitment example or another application of descending turn order.

findings.finding: All 53 literal stems and keys were checked. No additional concrete scenario is underdetermined on the supported domain explicitly asked. Q12 has four specified players and tied leaders, so neither majority bonus can change their keyed scores; Q13 explicitly asks for scoreboard points before bonuses. Q28 specifies the relevant court counts. Q31/Q32 explicitly supply eligible regions, avoiding the protected-only/no-eligible-region gap. Generic action descriptions do not independently settle unasked shortages.

All base card types and their explicit ordinary branches are represented. Source gaps cannot be converted into definitive expected answers or treated as solved by a coverage-map citation. Zero additional supported questions would still not establish complete-core gameplay.

proposed_additions.question: Which power cards does each player receive at setup?
proposed_additions.expected_answer: Each player takes the complete set of 13 power cards in that player’s color, numbered 1–13.
proposed_additions.prerequisites: None; this is the standard-game initial hand, before any power cards have been played.
proposed_additions.novelty: Tests starting availability of the complete power-card choice set; no current stem/key states that initial resource rule.

source_limits.case: The King returns when a player has fewer than three eligible own Caballeros across court and non-protected board regions.
source_limits.defined: Three own must return; source types and clockwise order are given.
source_limits.undefined: No less-than-three fallback; cannot assume remove all available, take protected pieces or omit a player.

source_limits.case: Actor-selected one Caballero per player when a player has no own Caballero in an eligible board region.
source_limits.defined: Actor chooses one for each player, including self; King region and Castillo excluded; no court source offered.
source_limits.undefined: No exemption or shortage procedure is stated.

source_limits.case: Secret removal of two with no legal occupied region, or a legal singleton region but multiple own Caballeros only in the protected King region.
source_limits.defined: Select a region with at least two; a singleton fallback exists when at most one is present in any region; King and Castillo may not supply pieces.
source_limits.undefined: The no-eligible-region case lacks a fallback; protected-only multi-piece holdings make the literal any-region singleton condition problematic. Actor disk participation also differs between fellow-player heading and all-player disk instruction.

source_limits.case: Secret return-all when own board pieces exist only in the King region.
source_limits.defined: Chosen region must contain at least one own; no-region-Caballero player is unaffected; protected pieces cannot be taken.
source_limits.undefined: No exemption for having pieces but none in an eligible region; all-player disk instruction versus fellow-player heading remains procedurally imprecise.

source_limits.case: Forced Movement destinations involving the Castillo.
source_limits.defined: General movement rule permits Castillo entry; this card requires each affected player to select another region on a disk, which excludes Castillo.
source_limits.undefined: No definitive reconciliation of the blanket Castillo-entry permission with the card-specific single disk-selected destination. Do not create a keyed Castillo destination ruling.

source_limits.case: All-4 special scoring after a 4/0/0 mobile scoreboard is placed at the Castillo.
source_limits.defined: Castillo may receive a mobile board; all-4 follows current scoreboard values; all-5 expressly excludes Castillo.
source_limits.undefined: All-4 does not expressly resolve whether the mobile-scored special location joins the region category. Neither inclusion nor exclusion is sufficiently definitive for a new key.

source_limits.case: The Court action when fewer than two own Caballeros remain in provinces.
source_limits.undefined: No explicit shortfall fallback, and power-card recruitment shortage permission is specifically attached to recruitment. Do not import that permission to this action.

source_limits.case: Players finish tied furthest along success track.
source_limits.undefined: No explicit tied-winner/tiebreak procedure. Q20 correctly repeats the published ordinary winner criterion without inventing one.
